title: The Shadowy Story of Oppenheimer and Congress

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Hollywood's award season is officially underway.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞颁奖季正式拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: Just the beginning of the fun and glamour of award season.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是颁奖季欢乐与魅力的开始。

sentences.en: Nominations for the Academy Awards, one of Hollywood's biggest events, were announced today.
sentences.zh: 好莱坞最盛大的活动之一——奥斯卡金像奖的提名名单今天公布了。

sentences.en: I think we had a Barbenheimer summer.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们度过了一个“芭比海默”之夏。

sentences.en: Oh, did we?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: It was so much fun.
sentences.zh: 那真的太有趣了。

sentences.en: Listen, Oppenheimer should lead the way.
sentences.zh: 听着，《奥本海默》理应领跑。

sentences.en: Oppenheimer right now is the movie to beat for the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 《奥本海默》现在是奥斯卡奖最有力的竞争者。

sentences.en: And one movie, Oppenheimer, about the father of the atomic bomb, topped the list with 13 nominations.
sentences.zh: 其中一部关于原子弹之父的电影《奥本海默》以13项提名高居榜首。

sentences.en: The film captured the imagination of millions of people last summer, including our congressional correspondent, Katie Edmondson.
sentences.zh: 这部电影去年夏天俘获了数百万人的想象力，其中就包括我们的国会记者凯蒂·埃德蒙森。

sentences.en: Today, Katie describes how Oppenheimer sent her on a quest to find the secret story of how Congress paid for the bomb and what that reveals about the inner workings of Washington.
sentences.zh: 今天，凯蒂将讲述《奥本海默》如何让她踏上一段探寻之旅，去揭开国会当年如何为原子弹买单的秘密，以及这揭示了华盛顿怎样的内部运作机制。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, January 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月23日，星期二。

sentences.en: Katie, you cover Congress for the Times, as our listeners, of course, know.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，正如我们的听众所知，你负责报道国会新闻。

sentences.en: But you join us today to talk about something a little out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 但你今天来是为了谈论一件有点不同寻常的事情。

sentences.en: A story which many of our listeners may not immediately associate with a Times congressional reporter.
sentences.zh: 一个许多听众可能不会立刻将其与《纽约时报》国会记者联系起来的故事。

sentences.en: And it has everything to do with the blockbuster movie Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 而这与那部大片《奥本海默》有着千丝万缕的联系。

sentences.en: So tell us how you ended up reporting this very unusual story.
sentences.zh: 那么，告诉我们你是如何开始报道这个非常不寻常的故事的吧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, it all started really when I went to go see Oppenheimer, like I'm assuming a lot of our listeners did over the summer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一切其实始于我去看《奥本海默》的时候，我想很多听众夏天也都去看了。

sentences.en: I was actually working in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 当时我其实在柏林工作。

sentences.en: I thought that I would get a little break from covering Congress.
sentences.zh: 我本以为能从报道国会的工作中稍微喘口气。

sentences.en: I knew that there was going to be a big spending fight in the fall.
sentences.zh: 我知道秋天会有一场关于预算的大战。

sentences.en: And I was kind of anxious to focus on something else for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时很想暂时专注于别的事情。

sentences.en: And so I went to this movie.
sentences.zh: 于是我就去看了这部电影。

sentences.en: We're at war, Hans.
sentences.zh: 我们在打仗，汉斯。

sentences.en: Which is, of course, about J.
sentences.zh: 电影当然是关于J·罗伯特·奥本海默的。

sentences.en: Robert Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·奥本海默。

sentences.en: Now let's calculate how much more destructive it would have been if it were a nuclear and not a chemical reaction.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们计算一下，如果这是核反应而不是化学反应，破坏力会大多少。

sentences.en: And the creation of the atomic bomb.
sentences.zh: 以及原子弹的制造过程。

sentences.en: Expressing power in terms of tons of TNT.
sentences.zh: 用TNT当量来表达威力。

sentences.en: But it would be thousands.
sentences.zh: 那将是数千吨。

sentences.en: Well then, kilotons.
sentences.zh: 那就叫千吨级吧。

sentences.en: And the movie takes place, or a lot of it takes place, in Los Alamos.
sentences.zh: 电影的故事发生地，或者说大部分场景，是在洛斯阿拉莫斯。

sentences.en: Physics and New Mexico, huh?
sentences.zh: 物理学和新墨西哥州，是吧？

sentences.en: My God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Which is this base that Oppenheimer and the military built up out of the desert, really out of nothing.
sentences.zh: 这就是奥本海默和军方在沙漠中建立的基地，真的是凭空建立起来的。

sentences.en: This way, gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 这边请，先生们。

sentences.en: This huge, sprawling base where scientists from across the country came.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的、蔓延开来的基地，来自全国各地的科学家汇聚于此。

sentences.en: To figure out how to build the bomb.
sentences.zh: 为了研究如何制造原子弹。

sentences.en: Dr. Lawrence.
sentences.zh: 劳伦斯博士。

sentences.en: Leslie.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利。

sentences.en: They had homes for the families of the scientists there.
sentences.zh: 他们还在那里为科学家的家属提供了住所。

sentences.en: There's no kitchen.
sentences.zh: 这里没有厨房。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Something that I couldn't stop thinking about while these scenes were flashing on screen was, this looks really expensive.
sentences.zh: 当这些画面在银幕上闪过时，我脑子里一直挥之不去的一个念头是：这看起来真贵啊。

sentences.en: Did Congress approve the money for that?
sentences.zh: 国会批准这笔钱了吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how much were they told?
sentences.zh: 如果批准了，他们被告知了多少？

sentences.en: Because another big theme of this movie was that this was a very secret project,
sentences.zh: 因为这部电影的另一个主题是，这是一个高度机密的项目，

sentences.en: that the number of people who knew about what was really happening at Los Alamos was extremely restricted.
sentences.zh: 知道洛斯阿拉莫斯真实情况的人数极其有限。

sentences.en: And so I was thinking, if that was true, how do you get Congress to approve what has to be a huge tranche of money to fund this thing?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就在想，如果这是真的，你是怎么让国会批准一笔必须是巨额的资金来资助这个项目的？

sentences.en: It was very much an intrusive thought that kept poking in throughout the movie.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个在观影过程中不断冒出来的侵入性想法。

sentences.en: Katie, you were in Berlin so that you weren't having to cover Congress.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你当时在柏林，所以你不需要报道国会。

sentences.en: But yet, there you were.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，你还是在那儿。

sentences.en: Your head was back in Congress.
sentences.zh: 你的心思又回到了国会。

sentences.en: You can take the girl out of Congress, but.
sentences.zh: 你可以让一个女孩离开国会，但是……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a little embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，有点尴尬。

sentences.en: So then what do you do?
sentences.zh: 那你后来做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I kind of just assumed that if I started Googling it, that I would come to some sort of quick answer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时想，如果我开始谷歌搜索，应该很快就能找到答案。

sentences.en: There's been so much research and so much academic work done on this period.
sentences.zh: 关于这一时期已经有了大量的研究和学术成果。

sentences.en: And I was surprised to find that there really wasn't that much.
sentences.zh: 但我惊讶地发现，其实并没有太多相关信息。

sentences.en: There were a few lines on Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 维基百科上只有寥寥几行。

sentences.en: I ended up finding a textbook that gave a sort of brief version of how Congress had sort of surreptitiously approved money in a bill.
sentences.zh: 我最终找到了一本教科书，里面简略地提到了国会是如何在法案中偷偷批准这笔资金的。

sentences.en: It was at the behest of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 这是在富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福总统的授意下进行的。
zh_words: 富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福

sentences.en: And as I was reading just these few kind of breadcrumbs, I just kept thinking, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 当我读到这些零星的线索时，我一直在想，这是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean Congress secretly passed this money and not a lot of people knew about it?
sentences.zh: 国会秘密通过了这笔钱，而且没多少人知道，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because, look, this is my job currently is to go through the spending bills, to look for things that are peculiar.
sentences.zh: 因为你看，我目前的工作就是审查支出法案，寻找那些奇怪的项目。

sentences.en: I also know that lawmakers are really bad at keeping secrets generally.
sentences.zh: 我也知道立法者通常很不擅长保守秘密。

sentences.en: And so the idea that this happened, this huge secret was smuggled through Congress without really anyone knowing, it just I just didn't see how that could be true.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个巨大的秘密在国会中被暗中通过，而几乎没人知道，我实在看不出这怎么可能是真的。

sentences.en: And this is not just like some dumb bridge or a road or something, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是什么愚蠢的桥梁或道路之类的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: It was a whole different scale, like it was ushering in the dawn of the atomic age.
sentences.zh: 这完全是另一个量级，它开启了原子时代的黎明。

sentences.en: Well, that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: And beyond the implications of the creation of this weapon of mass destruction, there's also the cost, right?
sentences.zh: 除了制造这种大规模杀伤性武器的影响外，还有成本问题，对吧？

sentences.en: The amount of money that Congress ultimately was asked to pass secretly was $800 million for this project, which in today's money is about $13 billion.
sentences.zh: 国会最终被要求秘密通过的金额是8亿美元，换算成今天的钱大约是130亿美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so every time I picked up on another little breadcrumb like this, I just became more incredulous.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我发现另一条小线索时，我就变得更加怀疑了。

sentences.en: Essentially, I wanted to understand even more how they were able to pull this off.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我更想了解他们到底是如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: And so I pitched to my editor, well, why don't I do, like, it'll be a fun historical memo that I'll write about this.
sentences.zh: 于是我向编辑提议，写一篇关于此事的历史备忘录，应该会很有趣。

sentences.en: And she agreed to let me do that.
sentences.zh: 她同意让我写了。

sentences.en: And so that really set off this kind of obsessive search to figure out the answer of exactly how Congress was able to secretly pass $800 million for the atomic bomb.
sentences.zh: 这真的开启了我那种执着的搜索，去弄清楚国会到底是如何秘密通过这8亿美元原子弹经费的。

sentences.en: Katie, I love your nerdiness.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，我喜欢你的书呆子劲儿。

sentences.en: So what did that obsessive search look like?
sentences.zh: 那么那次执着的搜索是什么样的？

sentences.en: Like, where did you start?
sentences.zh: 你是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Well, at this point, I was back in D.C.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那时我已经回到华盛顿了。

sentences.en: I had come back from Berlin.
sentences.zh: 我已经从柏林回来了。

sentences.en: And this ended up becoming very much a side project because there was actually a lot of spending drama happening here in D.C.
sentences.zh: 这最终变成了一个副业，因为当时华盛顿确实有很多支出方面的闹剧正在发生，

sentences.en: in real time that I was having to cover.
sentences.zh: 我必须实时报道这些。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But it took me through the digital archives of a lot of different libraries, former President Roosevelt's archives.
sentences.zh: 但这带我查阅了许多不同图书馆的数字档案，还有前总统罗斯福的档案。

sentences.en: And so it just kept happening that you would kind of get close to some sort of answer,
sentences.zh: 事情总是这样，你似乎快要接近答案了，

sentences.en: some sort of document that seemed like it would unlock the secret of this and you would get a few pieces.
sentences.zh: 找到了一些似乎能解开这个秘密的文件，你拼凑出了一些碎片。

sentences.en: But I was particularly obsessed with trying to get the account of one of the lawmakers who was physically in the room when these discussions were happening,
sentences.zh: 但我特别执着于试图找到当时身处讨论现场的某位立法者的陈述，

sentences.en: who was in the room when the decision was made.
sentences.zh: 也就是在做出决定时在场的人。

sentences.en: Because to me, that was just going to give me the most direct, the sharpest perspective of exactly how this worked.
sentences.zh: 因为对我来说，那将给我提供最直接、最敏锐的视角，了解这一切究竟是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I had a list of the seven lawmakers who were brought into this secret.
sentences.zh: 所以我列出了一份被纳入这个秘密的七位立法者的名单。

sentences.en: I knew that one of the lawmakers in one of these secret meetings was Sam Rayburn, who was the Speaker of the House at the time in 1944, considered one of the most famous,
sentences.zh: 我知道其中一次秘密会议的参与者之一是萨姆·雷伯恩，他是1944年当时的众议院议长，被认为是历史上最著名、

sentences.en: one of the most legendary House Speakers of all time.
sentences.zh: 最传奇的众议院议长之一。

sentences.en: And so I contacted the library where his papers are kept in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以我联系了位于德克萨斯州奥斯汀保存他文件的图书馆。

sentences.en: And I found out that those documents have not been digitized.
sentences.zh: 结果发现那些文件还没有被数字化。

sentences.en: They were sitting in folders, in boxes.
sentences.zh: 它们就放在文件夹里，装在盒子里。

sentences.en: And so, well, and so I struck up an acquaintance with a reference intern there, a very intrepid man named Deion Kaufman, who I'm so indebted to him for this because I kept saying,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我和那里的一位参考实习生建立了一种交情，一个非常勇敢的人，名叫迪恩·考夫曼，我非常感激他，因为我一直在问，

sentences.en: well, what about this folder and what about that folder?
sentences.zh: 这个文件夹里有什么？那个文件夹里有什么？

sentences.en: And he would go and he would look and it just did not yield anything.
sentences.zh: 他会去查看，但什么也没发现。

sentences.en: But at least I could sort of rest knowing that someone had physically paged through those folders.
sentences.zh: 但至少我可以安心了，因为我知道有人亲自翻阅过那些文件夹。

sentences.en: So I was still looking for a lawmaker in the room.
sentences.zh: 所以我还在寻找当时在场的立法者。

sentences.en: And then I found that one of them, a Senator, Elmer Thomas of Oklahoma, who had been invited to a secret briefing in the Senate about this whole gambit,
sentences.zh: 然后我发现其中一位，来自俄克拉荷马州的参议员埃尔默·托马斯，他曾被邀请参加参议院关于整个计划的秘密简报会，

sentences.en: had actually written a memoir.
sentences.zh: 他其实写过一本回忆录。

sentences.en: OK, so I've never heard of Elmer Thomas from Oklahoma or of his memoir.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我从没听说过俄克拉荷马州的埃尔默·托马斯，也没听说过他的回忆录。

sentences.en: How bad is that?
sentences.zh: 这很糟糕吗？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，没关系。

sentences.en: I hadn't either.
sentences.zh: 我以前也没听说过。

sentences.en: But it turns out he was actually a pretty important guy on Capitol Hill at the time when this all happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，在这一切发生时，他在国会山其实是个相当重要的人物。

sentences.en: He was the chairman of the Appropriations Subcommittee that oversaw military spending.
sentences.zh: 他是负责监督军事开支的拨款小组委员会主席。

sentences.en: And so he was one of just a few lawmakers who were brought into this secret.
sentences.zh: 所以他是少数几个被纳入这个秘密的立法者之一。

sentences.en: And it turns out his memoir, 40 years, a legislator, perhaps unsurprisingly, was not in wide circulation.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他的回忆录《40年立法者生涯》不出所料，并没有广泛流传。

sentences.en: But I did learn that there was a copy actually at the Library of Congress.
sentences.zh: 但我确实了解到国会图书馆有一本副本。

sentences.en: So I got my Library of Congress library card.
sentences.zh: 所以我办了国会图书馆的借书证。

sentences.en: And on a quiet day, I went over.
sentences.zh: 在一个安静的日子里，我过去了。

sentences.en: There are actually tunnels that connect the Capitol building to the Library of Congress.
sentences.zh: 其实有隧道连接着国会大厦和国会图书馆。

sentences.en: I kept getting loSt.
sentences.zh: 我一直迷路。

sentences.en: And so around the third time that I was trying to find the room where this book was, I was thinking, like, this is a lot of time now that I'm spending on this book that...
sentences.zh: 所以大约第三次试图找到存放这本书的房间时，我在想，我花在书上的时间太多了……

sentences.en: Your editor is basically tapping a foot.
sentences.zh: 你的编辑基本上已经在不耐烦地跺脚了。

sentences.en: Yeah, may or may not be helpful.
sentences.zh: 是啊，可能有用，也可能没用。

sentences.en: But I finally got the book.
sentences.zh: 但我终于拿到了那本书。

sentences.en: I opened it up and it was all there.
sentences.zh: 我翻开它，一切都在里面。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最优秀的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: So Katie, what was the story you ultimately pieced together?
sentences.zh: 那么凯蒂，你最终拼凑出的故事是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, how did they hide the building of the atomic bomb in the budget?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们是如何在预算中隐藏原子弹制造费用的？

sentences.en: So here's what I learned.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所了解到的。

sentences.en: Initially,
sentences.zh: 最初，

sentences.en: the way that Roosevelt officials were getting the money for the research to create the bomb was they were actually just taking money that Congress had appropriated under different lied items and they were funneling it to the Manhattan Project.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福政府官员获取研究资金以制造原子弹的方式，实际上只是挪用了国会在其他项目下拨出的款项，并将这些资金秘密输送给曼哈顿计划。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So skimming from other things, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就是从其他地方挪用资金。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是这样。

sentences.en: But by 1944, looking through the documents, it became very clear that Roosevelt himself, as well as his top officials,
sentences.zh: 但到了1944年，查阅相关文件后可以非常清楚地看到，罗斯福本人以及他的高层官员，

sentences.en: were growing very anxious about the idea of Nazi Germany maybe beating us to creating the atomic bomb.
sentences.zh: 对纳粹德国可能抢在我们前面造出原子弹的想法感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: I came across this memo from FDR to Vannevar Bush, who at that time was overseeing the administration of the Manhattan Project.
sentences.zh: 我偶然发现了富兰克林·罗斯福（FDR）写给万尼瓦尔·布什的一份备忘录，当时布什负责监管曼哈顿计划的行政工作。

sentences.en: And it was just one line.
sentences.zh: 那上面只有一行字。

sentences.en: And he wrote, do you have the money, FDR?
sentences.zh: 他写道：你有钱吗？——罗斯福。

sentences.en: So the administration essentially realizes Germany's close to getting the bomb.
sentences.zh: 所以政府基本上意识到德国快要造出原子弹了。

sentences.en: So time for some major money.
sentences.zh: 是时候筹集一大笔钱了。

sentences.en: Do you have it?
sentences.zh: 你有钱吗？

sentences.en: You know, that means Congress.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这意味着得找国会。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Only Congress has the power of the purse.
sentences.zh: 只有国会拥有拨款权。

sentences.en: And so they decided we have to ask Congress for a big infusion of cash now.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定，我们现在必须请求国会注入一大笔资金。

sentences.en: So that also means we have to tell members of Congress that we're doing this right.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着我们必须告诉国会议员我们正在做这件事。

sentences.en: We have to let them in on the secret.
sentences.zh: 我们必须让他们参与这个秘密。

sentences.en: And so Roosevelt gives the word to really his point man on this was Henry L.
sentences.zh: 于是罗斯福向他的关键人物传达了指示，这个人就是亨利·L·

sentences.en: Stimson, who was then the secretary of war.
sentences.zh: 史汀生，他当时担任战争部长。

sentences.en: And he says, I need you to tell a very small group of lawmakers exactly what's happening here.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福对他说，我需要你告诉一小部分议员这里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: I need you to get them to agree to pass this money.
sentences.zh: 我需要你让他们同意批准这笔资金。

sentences.en: And crucially, I need you to get them to keep it a secret.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，我需要你让他们保守秘密。

sentences.en: And so Stimson heads up to Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 于是史汀生前往国会山。

sentences.en: He has two separate secret meetings, one in the House, one in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他举行了两次单独的秘密会议，一次在众议院，一次在参议院。

sentences.en: In one particular meeting in the House, he actually brings George Marshall, the incredibly famous general,
sentences.zh: 在众议院的一次会议上，他甚至带上了极其著名的乔治·马歇尔将军，

sentences.en: to the meeting to kind of impress upon lawmakers just the seriousness of what he is asking them to do.
sentences.zh: 参加会议，以此向议员们强调他所要求他们做的事情的严重性。

sentences.en: And we know from Senator Elmer Thomas' memoir what their pitch was.
sentences.zh: 我们从埃尔默·托马斯参议员的回忆录中得知了他们的游说内容。

sentences.en: He writes that he received a call from the Senate majority leader saying, I'm inviting you to this secret meeting.
sentences.zh: 他写道，他接到了参议院多数党领袖的电话，说：我邀请你参加这个秘密会议。

sentences.en: You need to come to my office in an hour.
sentences.zh: 你一小时后必须到我的办公室来。

sentences.en: You cannot tell anyone where you are going or that you are going to a meeting at all.
sentences.zh: 你不能告诉任何人你要去哪里，或者你根本要去参加会议。

sentences.en: Keep it under wraps.
sentences.zh: 保密。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Elmer Thomas goes an hour later to the Senate majority leader's office.
sentences.zh: 一小时后，埃尔默·托马斯去了参议院多数党领袖的办公室。

sentences.en: It's just him, a couple other senators, and the war secretary, and a couple of his officers.
sentences.zh: 那里只有他、另外几位参议员、战争部长以及他的几名军官。

sentences.en: And in the meeting, Henry Stimson, the war secretary, tells these senators that the United States has been working on creating a bomb that can, quote,
sentences.zh: 在会议上，战争部长亨利·史汀生告诉这些参议员，美国一直在致力于制造一种炸弹，引用他的话，

sentences.en: do as much damage as 10,000 tons of any explosive known at that time.
sentences.zh: 其威力相当于当时已知任何爆炸物1万吨的破坏力。

sentences.en: And he writes that he recalls Stimson saying that the Germans are working on a weapon just like this, and that whoever is able to create this weapon first is going to win the war.
sentences.zh: 他写道，他记得史汀生说德国人正在研制同样的武器，谁能先造出这种武器，谁就能赢得战争。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so what does Elmer Thomas think about this?
sentences.zh: 那么埃尔默·托马斯对此有何看法？

sentences.en: What does he say?
sentences.zh: 他说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he writes in his memoir, this was something that absolutely floored him.
sentences.zh: 他在回忆录中写道，这件事让他彻底震惊了。

sentences.en: And so the impression that Thomas and the other senators get is that this is absolutely something that must be done,
sentences.zh: 所以托马斯和其他参议员得到的印象是，这绝对是必须要做的事情，

sentences.en: that must be kept a secret, and that they are going to go to any lengths that they can to pass this money.
sentences.zh: 必须保密，而且他们会不惜一切代价通过这笔资金。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this tiny group of lawmakers in Congress agreed to secretly fund this project.
sentences.zh: 所以国会中这一小群议员同意秘密资助这个项目。

sentences.en: But I guess the question remains, how do you do that?
sentences.zh: 但我猜问题依然存在，你们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How do you hide it?
sentences.zh: 你们怎么隐藏它？

sentences.en: Well, this is maybe my favorite part of the entire story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能是我整个故事中最喜欢的部分。

sentences.en: And it's something that Elmer Thomas's memoir, again, I love Elmer Thomas now in this memoir,
sentences.zh: 这再次出现在埃尔默·托马斯的回忆录中，我现在很喜欢埃尔默·托马斯的回忆录，

sentences.en: that he let us in on the secret, which is that they hid it essentially in an innocuous sounding line item.
sentences.zh: 他向我们透露了这个秘密，那就是他们基本上把它隐藏在一个听起来无关紧要的项目里。

sentences.en: I wasn't able to find a copy of the bill, but I did find a report from the hearing where they considered the bill.
sentences.zh: 我没能找到法案的副本，但我确实找到了他们审议该法案时的听证会报告。

sentences.en: And when you look through all of the different line items for the spending bill, I mean, they had the horses that they were going to use over in Italy, horses and donkeys.
sentences.zh: 当你查看支出法案中所有不同的项目时，我的意思是，他们有要在意大利使用的马匹，马和驴。

sentences.en: And then there was this one line item that said expediting production.
sentences.zh: 然后有这么一个项目写着：加速生产。

sentences.en: And that was the shell that they used to conceal this $800 million for the bomb, expediting production.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们用来掩盖这8亿美元炸弹资金的幌子，加速生产。

sentences.en: So that's some pretty bland language.
sentences.zh: 那确实是很平淡的措辞。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like a good disguise, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来是个很好的伪装，对吧？

sentences.en: You can completely see why it would not have raised any eyebrows at the time.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么它在当时不会引起任何人的怀疑。

sentences.en: There was a short description in that hearing report that said, well, you know, this is a line item intended to speed munitions to our boys in Europe
sentences.zh: 听证会报告中有一段简短的描述，说，嗯，你知道，这是一个旨在加快向我们在欧洲的士兵提供弹药的项目，

sentences.en: to make sure that we're using the most modern weapons on the battlefield possible, which is a huge understatement when you know what was actually hidden there.
sentences.zh: 以确保我们在战场上使用尽可能现代化的武器，当你了解那里实际上隐藏了什么时，这简直是极大的轻描淡写。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Katie, did anybody notice it?
sentences.zh: 那么凯蒂，有人注意到吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, there were a few close calls and one of them that was probably the most amusing to me
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，有几次差点露馅，其中一次可能是我觉得最有趣的，

sentences.en: actually came through in the form of an anecdote told by former Speaker Sam Rayburn, who told this story to a historian at his home in Texas many years after the fact.
sentences.zh: 实际上是以一则轶事的形式出现的，这是前众议院议长萨姆·雷伯恩在事发多年后，在他德克萨斯的家中告诉一位历史学家的。

sentences.en: He said that he was walking around one day shortly after that secret meeting with the war secretary
sentences.zh: 他说，在与战争部长举行那次秘密会议后不久的一天，他正在走动，

sentences.en: where the lawmakers all agreed to hide this money and that he saw one of the congressmen who had been in that meeting talking to a reporter.
sentences.zh: 当时议员们都同意隐藏这笔钱，他看到参加会议的一位国会议员正在和一名记者交谈。

sentences.en: And he said, the congressman, when I saw him, looked funny.
sentences.zh: 他说，我看到那位议员时，他看起来神色古怪。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: At least in Rayburn's interpretation, the congressman had been leaking the contents of this secret meeting to the newspaperman.
sentences.zh: 至少在雷伯恩看来，那位议员一直在向报社记者泄露这次秘密会议的内容。

sentences.en: And what does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, so Rayburn goes up to the newspaperman and he said, and this is what Rayburn recalled.
sentences.zh: 嗯，雷伯恩走到报社记者面前说，这是雷伯恩的回忆。

sentences.en: He went up to the newspaperman and said, you are a good American, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 他走到报社记者面前说：你是个好美国人，对吧？

sentences.en: You love your country.
sentences.zh: 你热爱你的国家。

sentences.en: The newspaperman said, of course.
sentences.zh: 报社记者说：当然。

sentences.en: Rayburn said, then don't print anything about what he just told you.
sentences.zh: 雷伯恩说：那就不要刊登任何关于他刚才告诉你的内容。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So the newspaperman caves, right?
sentences.zh: 所以报社记者屈服了，对吧？

sentences.en: How do you understand what happened here?
sentences.zh: 你如何理解这里发生的事情？

sentences.en: Well, I think you also have to understand the context of this time period, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你还必须理解那个时期的背景，对吧？

sentences.en: The United States was in this protracted war with Germany and with Japan.
sentences.zh: 美国当时正处于与德国和日本的长期战争中。

sentences.en: It was a time period where I think everyone, including the press, were being expected to sort of rally around the flag to support our troops.
sentences.zh: 那是一个我认为每个人，包括媒体，都被期望团结在国旗下支持我们军队的时期。

sentences.en: And so I think he was just let into a secret of the highest national security in a hallway by one member of Congress, only to be then abruptly headed off by the very powerful
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他只是在走廊里被一位国会议员告知了一个最高国家安全机密，随后又被非常有权势的

sentences.en: Speaker of the House who appeals to his sense of patriotism.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长突然拦住，并诉诸他的爱国主义感。

sentences.en: But I mean, this would have been an enormously difficult decision.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这本应是一个极其艰难的决定。

sentences.en: I mean, if I were that reporter now, this would be something that I would escalate up to
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我现在是那个记者，我会把这件事上报给

sentences.en: our highest editors and probably would be the subject of a really fierce debate at our newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我们最高级别的编辑，这很可能会成为我们报社内部激烈辩论的主题。

sentences.en: So it sounds like it was no small feat to keep this thing under wraps until, of course, it wasn't a secret and the whole world learned of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来要保守这个秘密并非易事，当然，直到它不再是秘密，全世界在得知美国

sentences.en: atomic program in, you know, shocking detail when the United States dropped the bomb on Hiroshima.
sentences.zh: 在广岛投下原子弹时，才以令人震惊的细节了解了美国的原子能计划。

sentences.en: What was it like, Katie, to be doing this congressional historical sleuthing, you know, uncovering all
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，进行这种国会历史侦探工作，揭开这一切

sentences.en: of this maneuvering in the 1940s, while at the same time covering Congress over the past year?
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代的政治操弄，同时在过去一年里报道国会，是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Any conclusions you draw from the comparison?
sentences.zh: 你从这种比较中得出了什么结论吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, since the story has come out, the question that I've gotten from a lot of readers
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，自从这个故事曝光以来，我从很多读者那里得到的问题是，

sentences.en: is, and I think this is what you're driving at, could something like this happen today?
sentences.zh: 我想这也是你想要探讨的，今天还会发生这样的事情吗？

sentences.en: Could a few members of Congress today hide some sort of big program or top secret activity within the spending bills?
sentences.zh: 今天有几位国会议员能在支出法案中隐藏某种大型项目或绝密活动吗？

sentences.en: And I found a number of interviews from some of the participants in the Manhattan Project that were done years after we bombed Hiroshima.
sentences.zh: 我找到了曼哈顿计划的一些参与者在广岛原子弹爆炸多年后接受的多次采访。

sentences.en: And the answer they gave was that they didn't think it would be possible to hide a program or a project of that magnitude
sentences.zh: 他们给出的答案是，他们认为不可能隐藏如此规模的项目或计划，

sentences.en: outside the context of a huge war at a time when there was this sense of patriotism among so many people.
sentences.zh: 除非是在一场大规模战争的背景下，且当时人们普遍具有这种爱国主义精神。

sentences.en: But look, I currently cover federal spending, and I do read through the spending bills that are passed into law.
sentences.zh: 但你看，我目前负责报道联邦支出，我确实会通读那些通过成为法律的支出法案。

sentences.en: And these are bills that are typically hundreds, if not thousands of pages long.
sentences.zh: 这些法案通常有数百甚至数千页长。

sentences.en: They are written in extremely archaic, dense legislative language.
sentences.zh: 它们是用极其古老、晦涩的立法语言编写的。

sentences.en: And I look through trying to see if there's any programs that seem peculiar or strange or warrant sort of greater investigation as to what they're doing in that spending bill.
sentences.zh: 我翻阅这些法案，试图看看是否有任何项目看起来很特殊、很奇怪，或者值得对它们在支出法案中的目的进行更深入的调查。

sentences.en: But the phrase expediting production, I mean, it's so innocuous.
sentences.zh: 但“加速生产”这个词，我的意思是，它太无害了。

sentences.en: If I were a reporter back in 1944 coming through that bill, I don't think it would have caused me to raise any eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 如果我是1944年的一名记者，翻阅那份法案，我认为它不会引起我的任何怀疑。

sentences.en: I think I would have read it and thought, yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我想我会读到它并认为，是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: Of course, we're trying to send weapons more quickly over to Europe.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们正试图更快地向欧洲运送武器。

sentences.en: And so I do think kind of the moral of that story, if there is one, is that just a few lawmakers can hide something like this if there's the will to do so.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这个故事的寓意，如果有什么寓意的话，那就是只要有心，少数议员就能隐藏这样的事情。

sentences.en: Katie, thank you.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Monday, the Supreme Court sided with the Biden administration, allowing federal authorities to cut or remove parts of a concertina wire barrier
sentences.zh: 周一，最高法院站在拜登政府一边，允许联邦当局切割或拆除部分铁丝网屏障，

sentences.en: along the Mexican border that Texas erected to keep migrants from crossing into the state.
sentences.zh: 这是德克萨斯州沿着墨西哥边境竖立的，旨在阻止移民进入该州。

sentences.en: The ruling, by a 5-4 vote, was a temporary measure that lifted a lower court's ban on removing the wire while it considered the case.
sentences.zh: 这项裁决以5比4的投票结果通过，是一项临时措施，解除了下级法院在审理此案期间禁止拆除铁丝网的禁令。

sentences.en: The justices gave no reason for their decision, which is typical when they act on such emergency applications.
sentences.zh: 大法官们没有说明他们做出这一决定的理由，这在他们处理此类紧急申请时是很典型的。

sentences.en: The ruling was a victory for the Biden administration in the increasingly bitter dispute between the White House and Governor Greg Abbott of Texas,
sentences.zh: 这项裁决是拜登政府在白宫与德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特之间日益激烈的争端中的一次胜利，

sentences.en: an outspoken critic of President Biden's border policy.
sentences.zh: 阿博特是拜登总统边境政策的直言不讳的批评者。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko and Ricky Nowetsky.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科和里基·诺韦茨基制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George and Lexi Diao, contains original music by Rowan

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场痛苦、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在此过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
